target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now work through Signal-owned reply-author resolution instead of adding a shared `replyToAuthor` field to every outbound channel path. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies record the inbound Signal sender by conversation and message timestamp so later Signal sends can attach the native quote metadata.

The only core behavior change is scoped to Signal send actions: when the Signal message action receives an explicit `replyToId`, it is treated as the reply target and wins over an inline `[[reply_to:...]]` directive.

## What Changed

- Signal outbound sends: message adapter, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal inbound messages: accepted inbound messages register `{account, conversation, message timestamp} -> sender author` for Signal group native reply lookup.
- Signal reply-author lookup: new Signal helper keeps a bounded in-process author cache and uses the existing optional Signal runtime store hook when available.
- Signal message action: `replyToId` is accepted as a Signal-only alias for explicit reply targets, and explicit `replyToId` wins over inline reply directives.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` derive native quote authors as `+15551234567` and `username:alice`.
- Group Signal replies resolve the quote author from the Signal-owned author cache instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Signal inbound context tests prove a group message stores the sender author under its Signal message timestamp.
- Signal message-action tests prove `replyToId` is only treated as an alias for the Signal channel.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior on head `878a45d2f0480a9612d63c294ecf45da3a3c0a4d`:

- `python3 /Users/jmerhi/repos/skills/skills/pr-proof-pack/scripts/pr_net_diff.py --markdown` reports base `origin/main 7e0324263b86`, head `878a45d2f048`, and lists the previous shared outbound/channel/queue/durable files as branch-only churn with no net diff.
- `git diff --check` passed locally.
- Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox `tbx_01kx12k2y2jks6j8fr4v3wbvtw` (`silver-krill`) passed `corepack pnpm test extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts`.
- Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox `tbx_01kx14hckaswjqgjnr1jah2ved` (`violet-lobster`) passed `corepack pnpm check:changed`.

Review note: this refresh intentionally removes the earlier broad shared `replyToAuthor` SDK/outbound/queue/durable plumbing from the net diff. Native Codex review was attempted earlier but the review service returned `429 Too Many Requests`, so it is not listed as completed proof.
